lines: Jamie Alvarez
+1 (555) 010-5820 | jamie.alvarez@example.com | example.com/in/jalvarez
Date of birth: 14 Nov 1995 | Nationality: Mexican
EDUCATION
Riverbend Polytechnic | B.S. in Industrial Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2014 - May 2018
EXPERIENCE
Crestway Foods | Supply Chain Planner | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Jul 2025
- Cut inbound freight cost per pallet from $48 to $41 over two quarters by consolidating supplier pickups into four regional milk runs.
- Set safety stock for all 1,400 SKUs with the economic order quantity (EOQ) formula, balancing ordering and holding costs.
- Built the weekly supplier scorecard for 40 vendors, which buyers used to renegotiate delivery windows with the five least reliable.
- Led the monthly sales and operations planning meeting, reconciling the sales forecast with plant capacity for the finance and production teams.
- Cut average order lead time through the warehouse from 10 days to 5 while holding daily throughput constant and doubling work-in-process to keep pickers busy.
- Rebuilt weekly demand planning for 1,400 SKUs across 3 distribution centers with a seasonal forecast model, cutting stockouts from 6.2% to 2.8% while inventory fell by $1.9M.
Lakeview Distribution | Operations Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2018 - Jan 2021
- Redesigned the pick paths for the fast-moving zone, cutting walking distance per order by 28% and raising picks per labor hour from 92 to 110.
- Ran a time study of the returns desk; the findings led to a triage station that cut returns processing time from 3 days to 1.
- Wrote the dock scheduling rules for 12 carriers, cutting average trailer wait at the dock from 95 to 40 minutes.

- Set up cycle counting for the 2,000 highest-value locations while also covering night-shift supervision, updating the safety training slides, coordinating holiday temp hiring and running the forklift certification schedule, which raised inventory record accuracy from 91% to 98.5%.
PROJECTS
Last-Mile Routing Study | Independent Project | Python | Oct 2024 - Present
- Spearheaded a data-driven, optimization-first transformation of last-mile logistics that unlocked significant efficiency gains.
- Cut average route length from 120 to 90 miles, a 40% reduction, by solving the routing problem with customer time windows.
- Shared the model and a one-page summary with the grocer's dispatch team, who piloted the routes on two trucks for a month.
Regional Food Bank Warehouse | Volunteer Consultant, Team of 4 | Excel | Mar 2022 - Jul 2022
- Re-slotted the food bank's dry-goods warehouse by turnover, cutting volunteer picking time per pantry order from 25 to 15 minutes.
- Mapped the donation intake process with the warehouse lead and removed two duplicate data-entry steps, so donations reached the shelves a day sooner.
- Built a seasonal forecast for 1,400 products across three warehouses that more than halved stockouts and cut inventory by nearly $2M.
SKILLS
Tools: Excel, Python, SAP
Methods: demand forcasting, inventory planning, time studies, vehicle routing

items.says: Replace placeholder contact details and make sure the profile URL leads to your actual profile.
items.because: These details need to be usable before applying.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality for most U.S. applications.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary and can invite bias.

items.says: Consider dropping the education start date.
items.because: The graduation year is usually sufficient.

items.says: Check whether the education location is useful.
items.because: It may just take up space.

items.says: Add shipment volume or annual savings if available.
items.because: The $7-per-pallet change needs business context.

items.says: EOQ is not a formula for setting safety stock.
items.because: EOQ addresses order quantity, not safety-stock levels.

items.says: Clarify whether the renegotiated windows improved delivery reliability.
items.because: The line shows use of the scorecard but not its outcome.

items.says: Add a concrete decision or result from the planning meeting if substantiated.
items.because: “Led” and “reconciling” describe responsibility more than impact.

items.says: Doubling work-in-process at constant throughput conflicts with halving lead time.
items.because: It would generally increase, not halve, flow time.

items.says: Clarify what the lead-time, throughput, and work-in-process measures represent.
items.because: The measures and causal explanation need rechecking.

items.says: Verify that the stockout and inventory changes are attributable to the demand-planning work.
Define the stockout measure.
items.because: A reader could interpret 6.2% in multiple ways.

items.says: Clarify your role in implementing the triage station if you did more than conduct the study.
Add the measurement period if it helps show the improvement was sustained.
Split or trim the cycle-counting line and its other duties.
items.because: The other tasks obscure the cycle-counting result.

items.says: Clarify which work raised inventory record accuracy.
items.because: The listed duties make the source of the improvement unclear.

items.says: Confirm that “Present” still reflects active work.
Clarify the relationship with the grocer.
items.because: “Independent Project” and a dispatch-team pilot need to make sense together.

items.says: Remove the broad “Spearheaded” line.
items.because: Its efficiency claim lacks evidence and is weaker than the specific results below it.

items.says: The route-length reduction is 25%, not 40%.
items.because: The distance fell from 120 to 90 miles.

items.says: Say whether the route-length figures came from a model, the pilot, or actual operations.
items.because: Those are materially different claims.

items.says: Add the pilot’s observed outcome if available.
items.because: Modeled savings should not be implied to have been proven by the pilot.

items.says: Confirm that the before-and-after picking times were measured comparably.
Clarify whether “a day sooner” was measured or estimated.
The food-bank forecast looks like an accidental duplicate of the Crestway result.
items.because: The product and warehouse counts, stockout improvement, and inventory reduction closely mirror it.

items.says: Specify the SAP module if your experience is substantial.
items.because: The module may be more informative than the platform name alone.

items.says: “Forcasting” is misspelled.
Standardize date dashes, capitalization, and line wrapping.
Put the most relevant and strongest results first within each role.
items.because: The duties should not all be treated equally.
